title: Discovered attacks
objectives: Recognize when one of your pieces is blocking a longer-range attack from another piece behind it
Play a move that both captures material and uncovers a discovered check at the same time
Recognize a discovered attack that isn't check, just a threat on a piece
Play a discovered check delivered by a different piece than the one that moves

steps.text: A discovered attack happens when a piece moves out of the way and unmasks an attack from a completely different piece behind it. Here, the knight on d4 is blocking the bishop's view of the king on h8. The moment the knight moves — to do anything at all — the bishop delivers check. The moving piece is free to capture something, attack something else, or do anything useful, while the piece it uncovers does the real damage.

steps.prompt: A discovered attack always has to be a discovered check.

feedback.default: A discovered attack can uncover an attack on anything — a rook, a queen, an undefended pawn — not only the king. It's called a discovered check specifically when the piece behind is the king; that's just the sharpest, most forcing version.

steps.successExplanation: Right — discovered check is the most forcing version, but a discovered attack can uncover an attack on any piece, not just the king.

steps.prompt: What makes a discovered check especially dangerous compared to an ordinary check?
options: It doesn't — all checks are equally dangerous
The piece that moves is completely free to do anything else useful — capture, attack, even deliver a second check of its own — while the discovered piece still gives check
It can only be delivered by a queen
It always ends the game immediately

feedback.default: The defining danger of a discovered check is that the moving piece isn't 'spent' giving the check — the check comes from the piece staying behind, so the moving piece gets to do something else entirely, for free.

steps.successExplanation: Right — the moving piece is completely free to capture or attack, since the check itself comes from the piece left behind.

steps.prompt: Move the knight to capture the bishop — notice what your rook can suddenly see once the knight is out of the way.

hints.text: Your knight is sitting on the same file as your rook and the enemy king. What happens the moment it moves?
The bishop is undefended and reachable in one jump.
Nxc7 wins the bishop, and moving the knight off the d-file uncovers a discovered check from your rook — Black must deal with the king first, and you've already banked the piece.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the bishop. Look for the knight move that captures it — then notice what opens up behind the knight.

steps.successExplanation: Nxc7 wins the bishop, and moving the knight off the d-file uncovers a discovered check from your rook — Black must deal with the king first, and you've already banked the piece.

steps.prompt: Capture the pawn with your knight — see what your rook attacks once the file opens up.

hints.text: The knight is blocking your rook's view down the d-file — what's sitting on that file, behind the knight?
The pawn is undefended and reachable in one jump.
Nxc6 wins the pawn, and moving the knight off the d-file uncovers your rook's attack on the enemy rook on d8 — not check this time, but a genuine threat Black has to answer.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the pawn. Find the knight's capture, and pay attention to what it uncovers behind it.

steps.successExplanation: Nxc6 wins the pawn for free. Moving the knight off the d-file uncovers your rook's attack on the rook on d8 — a discovered attack that isn't check, just a serious threat on top of the material you already won.

steps.prompt: Capture the pawn with your knight and watch what happens along the long diagonal.

hints.text: Your knight sits on the long diagonal between your queen and the enemy king. What happens once it moves anywhere?
The pawn is undefended and reachable in one jump.
Nxb5 wins the pawn, and clearing the long diagonal uncovers a discovered check from your queen — a different piece than the knight delivering it, exactly the point of a discovered attack.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the pawn. Find the knight's capture, then notice what your queen sees once the diagonal is clear.

steps.successExplanation: Nxb5 wins the pawn, and clearing the diagonal uncovers a discovered check from your queen on the far side of the board — the knight did the capturing, but a completely different piece delivers the check.

steps.summary: A discovered attack happens when moving one piece unmasks an attack from a piece behind it — and the moving piece is completely free to do something else useful in the process: capture material, create a second threat, even give a check of its own. When the uncovered attack lands on the enemy king, it's a discovered check — the sharpest version, since the opponent must respond to it immediately no matter what the moving piece just did. Before moving any piece, check whether it's blocking a longer-range attack from something behind it.
